What is Wilmington, Delaware like for a home seller?

Wilmington is the largest city in Delaware and the county seat of New Castle County, sitting where the Christina River and Brandywine Creek meet before reaching the Delaware River. It is about 33 miles southwest of Philadelphia, and the Census Bureau's 2020 count was 70,898 residents.

That count is far below the city's peak of 112,504 in 1940. Interstate 95 cut through neighborhoods when it was built in the 1950s and the city lost population for decades afterward. A seller today is working inside a housing stock that is old, varied and sometimes uneven from one block to the next.

The city lists more than 50 named neighborhoods, from Center City, Riverfront and Quaker Hill to Wawaset Park, Brandywine Village and The Flats. It also designates nine historic districts and one conservation district (Forty Acres). If your house is inside one of them, exterior changes can involve extra review, so ask the city before you start a repair project meant to help a sale.

How did Wilmington grow, and why does the history matter to a house?

Swedish colonists founded Fort Christina in March 1638, and the settlement was incorporated as Willingtown in 1731, took the name Wilmington with a borough charter in 1739, and received its city charter on March 7, 1832. DuPont began making gunpowder near the Brandywine in 1802, and the mills and shipyards that followed shaped the street grid and the rowhouse blocks you still see.

Many Wilmington houses are rowhouses or twins built for mill and shipyard workers. Older construction often means plaster walls, original wiring, steam or hot water heat, and basements that have seen water. Those are the items a buyer's inspector usually flags first, and they are also the ones that make a financed sale fall apart late in the process.

The Riverfront, once a shipbuilding and manufacturing area, saw state-sponsored renewal beginning in the late 1990s. The city's Riverwalk runs 1.2 miles, and the convention center and ballpark there anchor a different kind of neighborhood from the older residential blocks inland.

What jobs and employers shape Wilmington's housing demand?

Wilmington's economy leans on banking, health care, chemicals and state government. The Financial Center Development Act of 1981 removed interest rate caps and made the city a base for credit card operations, and the Delaware Court of Chancery and the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware are both located here.

The largest employers listed for 2019 show how broad the base is:

Employer (2019)Employees listed
State of Delaware14,199
ChristianaCare11,308
University of Delaware4,493
Amazon4,300
Nemours Children's Health3,795
DuPont3,500

Wilmington Trust is headquartered at Rodney Square, and Chemours, Corteva and Incyte also have a presence. For a seller, this mix means a steady pool of workers who need housing near downtown, but it does not change the fact that each house sells on its own condition and location.

What does Wilmington's climate and flood history mean for a house?

Wilmington has a humid subtropical climate with hot summers, cool to cold winters and about 45.33 inches of precipitation a year, spread fairly evenly through the months. Average annual snowfall is 20.2 inches, and about 21 days a year reach 90 degrees or higher.

Flooding is the weather issue that most affects a sale. In September 2021 the remnants of Hurricane Ida flooded hundreds of buildings and displaced dozens of families in the city. Delaware's floodplain engineer noted that FEMA maps reflect historic risk and do not account for future climate change, and that most homeowners and renters policies do not cover flood damage.

  • Check the FEMA flood zone for your parcel before you set a price or timeline.
  • Gather any flood insurance claims, repair receipts and drainage work for the buyer.
  • Expect inspectors to look hard at basements, sump pumps and foundation walls.
  • Tell buyers what you know. Delaware's seller disclosure law requires it, as covered below.

How do Wilmington property taxes work when you sell?

Wilmington bills city property tax, while New Castle County sets the assessed value and the school district sets its own tax. For fiscal year 2026 the city's rates were $3.7413 per $1,000 of assessed value for residential property and $5.8276 per $1,000 for non-residential property, which the city said together raise the same total revenue as the year before.

The county completed its first countywide reassessment since 1983, and the city said its FY2026 amounts rest on that work. Bills were mailed July 18, 2025, with the city portion due September 30, 2025 and county and school taxes due November 30, 2025. The city also announced an interior reassessment program on September 25, 2025 for neighborhoods with large assessment increases, and said the interior assessors would not report code violations.

ItemDetail from the city
Residential rate, FY2026$3.7413 per $1,000
Non-residential rate, FY2026$5.8276 per $1,000
City bills mailedJuly 18, 2025
City payment dueSeptember 30, 2025
Senior exemptionFirst $210,300 of assessed value, income limits apply, applications due May 16

Taxes are normally prorated at settlement, so a seller who has not paid the current bill usually has it taken from proceeds. The city said the residential rate would likely change the following year, so check the current bill at the city's property tax page before you do the math.

What does a Wilmington sale cost in transfer tax and closing steps?

Delaware's realty transfer tax is normally 4 percent of the value, made up of 2.5 percent state tax and 1.5 percent county or municipal tax, and the statute apportions it equally between seller and buyer. The state's own instructions describe the 1.5 percent as the county or municipality portion, and Wilmington has its own realty transfer tax rules in Chapter 44, Article IV of the city code.

The city's exemption affidavit lists categories such as foreclosure, divorce, mortgage default, governmental transfers and parent and child. A first-time buyer exemption in the city requires that the buyer has held no legal interest in residential real estate in Wilmington for at least three years and intends to occupy the home within 90 days.

  • A Delaware-licensed attorney must conduct the settlement. The Delaware Supreme Court's 2000 Mid-Atlantic Settlement Services decision and a September 22, 2006 order treat closings as the practice of law.
  • Under 30 Del. C. 5402, a first-time buyer's share can drop by 0.5 percent of the first $400,000 of value, a reduction of up to $2,000. The seller's share is unchanged.
  • Nonresident individual sellers must send estimated tax on the gain, 6.6 percent for individuals, with Form REW EST when the deed is presented for recording.

What rental license and vacancy rules affect Wilmington sellers?

Owners of rental property in Wilmington must hold a Residential Property Rental License, renewed annually under city code section 5-92, and newly acquired rentals must be registered with the Department of Licenses and Inspections. Buyers and sellers may be asked for proof of the transaction. Inspections run on a two or five year cycle depending on the number of units.

If you inherited a house or the last tenant left, vacancy can cost more than people expect. The city's vacant property fee depends on how many years a property has been vacant, regardless of ownership changes:

Years vacantAnnual fee
Less than 1$0
1$500
2$1,000
3 to 4$2,000
5 to 9$3,500
10$5,000, plus $500 for each year after

Owners must tell the department within 30 days of a sale or a change of mailing address, and failure to register can bring a fine of up to $500 or a civil action. Ask the city for a payoff figure early so no surprise lands at closing.

What must a Wilmington seller disclose?

Under the Delaware Buyer Property Protection Act, a seller of residential property with one to four units must disclose all known material defects in writing, and the Seller's Disclosure of Real Property Condition Report must go to buyers before they make an offer. Section 2572 requires the disclosure before the listing agreement is signed and requires updates for material changes before settlement.

Section 2577 exempts several kinds of transfers, including those made under a court order in an estate, trust or guardianship, deeds in lieu of foreclosure, sheriff's sales, and transfers between co-owners or to a spouse or lineal relative. If you are selling as an executor or after a foreclosure filing, ask your attorney which side of that line you sit on.

How does selling to a cash buyer compare with listing in Wilmington?

A cash sale removes the mortgage approval and appraisal steps, so closing can move on the seller's schedule once title is clear. A traditional listing exposes the house to more buyers but adds showings, buyer repair requests and the chance that financing fails.

Neither path avoids the Delaware attorney closing, the transfer tax split or the need to pay off city charges. We buy houses as-is, and we do not promise a price before we have seen the property. If an offer does not suit you, you owe nothing.

More questions about Wilmington, DE

How much is the realty transfer tax when selling a house in Wilmington?

It is normally 4 percent of the property value, with 2.5 percent going to the state and 1.5 percent to the local government, and Delaware law apportions it equally between seller and buyer. Wilmington has its own transfer tax rules in Chapter 44, Article IV of the city code, so confirm your exact figure with your closing attorney.

Do I need an attorney to sell my house in Wilmington?

Yes. Delaware requires a Delaware-licensed attorney to conduct real estate settlements, based on the Delaware Supreme Court's 2000 Mid-Atlantic Settlement Services decision and its September 22, 2006 order.

When are Wilmington city property taxes due?

For fiscal year 2026 the city mailed bills on July 18, 2025 and set the city payment deadline at September 30, 2025, with county and school taxes due November 30, 2025. Check the city's property tax page for the current year's dates.

What happens if my Wilmington house has been empty for years?

The city charges a vacant property fee that grows with each year of vacancy, from $0 under one year to $5,000 at ten years, plus $500 for each extra year. The fee follows the property, so it continues even if ownership changes.

Can I sell a Wilmington house that has flood damage?

Yes, but you must disclose known material defects in writing under 6 Del. C. 2572. Gather repair records and insurance claims, since most homeowners policies do not cover flood damage.

Where is Dover, Delaware, and how is it laid out?

Dover is the capital of Delaware and the county seat of Kent County, on the St. Jones River in the Delaware River coastal plain at roughly 30 feet above sea level. It is the state's second-largest city after Wilmington, and the Dover metro area covers all of Kent County.

The city is flat and spread out along a few main roads. U.S. Route 13 runs north and south as the Dupont Highway commercial strip, and US 13 Alternate passes through downtown on Governors Avenue. DE 1 is a toll road east of downtown that leads to Wilmington and the beaches, DE 8 runs east and west on Division Street, and DE 15 runs through the western side. Dover is one of only four state capitals without an Interstate highway.

If you are selling here, location relative to those roads matters to buyers more than a neighborhood name does. A house near DE 1 or the base reads differently to a commuter than one on a quiet street near the Green.

What is the history of Dover and why does it matter to older homes?

William Penn founded Dover in 1683 as the court town for the new Kent County, and the General Assembly had the town officially laid out in 1717. The state capital moved from New Castle to Dover in 1777, and the Assembly settled here permanently in October 1781.

The Green, a central square, holds the Kent County Courthouse and the Delaware Supreme Court. Twenty sites in Dover are on the National Register of Historic Places, including the Dover Green and Victorian Dover historic districts.

Owners of older houses downtown can face design review for exterior work, and the city publishes historic district guidelines. If your house sits near the Green, ask the city's planning office whether a planned repair needs approval before you spend money on it for a sale.

Which employers drive Dover's housing market?

State government is Dover's largest employer, with Kent County government also a major one, and Dover Air Force Base is the other pillar. The base lies in the southeast of the city and hosts two airlift wings and the military's only mortuary in the continental United States.

The Air Force's fiscal year 2023 estimate of the base's economic impact puts the numbers in perspective:

Dover AFB, FY23 estimateFigure
Total economic impact$891 million
Total jobs created8,969
Active duty personnel3,727
Total military and civilian personnel6,096
Total personnel including dependents8,514

Other employers include Kraft Foods and Procter and Gamble plants, and Delaware State University, Delaware Technical Community College's Terry Campus and Wesley College's former campus (now a Delaware State University downtown campus) add education jobs. Military assignments change on a schedule, so some Dover owners must sell on short notice when orders arrive. A cash sale can fit that kind of deadline.

What does Dover's weather mean for your roof and house?

Dover has a humid subtropical climate. Summers are hot and humid with about 25 days a year at or above 90 degrees, and winters are moderate, with annual precipitation averaging about 47.61 inches and snowfall about 13.2 inches that rarely stays long.

Wind is the more specific risk. Tropical Storm Isaias produced an EF2 tornado on August 4, 2020 that crossed the state, with damage in Dover rated EF1. Roof condition, siding and trees close to the house are worth documenting for that reason.

  • Document roof age and any storm repairs, since buyers and insurers ask.
  • Check the city's floodplain management page for your parcel, because Dover sits along the St. Jones River.
  • Keep records of any HVAC replacement, as humid summers put heavy load on cooling systems.

Which school districts serve Dover?

The Capital School District serves most of Dover and includes Dover High School, while the Caesar Rodney School District serves the southern part of the city and includes Caesar Rodney High School in Camden. Polytech School District operates a vocational-technical program with Polytech High School in Woodside.

Buyers with children often ask which district a house falls in, so have the answer ready. The school district is also the main force behind the school portion of the tax bill, which Kent County collects.

How are Dover property taxes billed?

Dover taxes you twice, once for the city and once through Kent County, and the two bills run on different calendars. The city's rate is $0.485 per $100 of assessed value, applied to values set at 100 percent of January 1, 2020 fair market value, and the city revalues all property every five years, last in 2020. City bills are mailed July 1, with supplemental bills in the first week of October, January and April. The assessment register is on display each April 1, and the 2026 appeal deadline was April 30 at 5:00 p.m., with no postmarks accepted.

Kent County's tax year runs June 1 to May 31. The county's last reassessment took effect July 1, 2023, and bills are usually mailed by mid-August, with the entire annual tax due by September 30. A sale does not trigger a reassessment.

ItemCity of DoverKent County
Rate or basis$0.485 per $100Set by school district, county and library
Bills mailedJuly 1Usually mid-August
Last revaluation2020July 1, 2023
AppealsApril 30, 2026 deadlineJanuary 31 for annual assessments

City tax office contact is 302-736-7005, and the county assessment office is at 555 Bay Road, Dover, phone 302-744-2401.

What transfer tax and recording steps apply to a Dover sale?

Delaware's realty transfer tax normally totals 4 percent, with 2.5 percent to the state and 1.5 percent to the local government, and the buyer and seller split it equally unless they agree otherwise. A first-time homebuyer can cut the buyer's share by 0.5 percent of up to $400,000, a reduction of at most $2,000.

Deeds for Dover property are recorded with the Kent County Recorder of Deeds at 555 Bay Road. The recorder says a deed cannot be recorded until fees and taxes are collected, and forms with errors can draw a $40 nonconforming fee or a $20 rejection fee. Your attorney will handle this, since Delaware requires an attorney to conduct the settlement.

The county ordinance for unincorporated areas sets a 1.5 percent transfer tax, but Dover is a city, so confirm with your attorney which local tax applies to a property within city limits.

What rental and vacancy rules should a Dover seller know?

Dover requires an annual rental dwelling permit that expires every January 31, and owners who live outside Kent County must have a property manager located in the county. If you are selling a rental house, make sure the permit and any fees are settled before closing.

Short-term rentals of less than 30 days are limited. Under the city's 2021 ordinance, the owner must be a Dover resident and may only offer a primary residence, with an annual license that is void on transfer of ownership.

  • The vacant building article of the city code defines a building as vacant when unoccupied for more than three consecutive months in the text posted by the city.
  • Owners must register within 30 days after a building becomes vacant, and report changes within 30 days.
  • Unpaid vacant building fees can be added to the tax bill, and the city can require payment before title transfers.

Confirm the current text and fees with the city's planning office, since the posted ordinance shows amendments in progress.

What disclosures does Delaware require from Dover sellers?

Sellers of residential property with one to four units must give a written disclosure of known material defects and the Seller's Disclosure of Real Property Condition Report before the buyer makes an offer. Exemptions in section 2577 cover estate, trust and guardianship transfers, deeds in lieu of foreclosure, sheriff's sales and transfers between relatives.

We buy Dover houses as-is, which means you can skip repairs, but the disclosure duty and the attorney closing still apply to the sale.

More questions about Dover, DE

How long does a house sale take in Dover, Delaware?

It depends on the route. A cash sale can close as soon as the title work and the attorney settlement are ready, while a financed sale also needs appraisal and loan approval. Delaware requires an attorney to conduct the settlement either way.

When are Dover city property tax bills due?

Dover mails city tax bills on July 1, with supplemental bills in the first week of October, January and April. Kent County bills are usually mailed by mid-August and the annual tax is due by September 30.

Where are deeds recorded for a Dover house?

Deeds are recorded with the Kent County Recorder of Deeds at 555 Bay Road in Dover. The recorder will not record a deed until the correct fees and taxes are collected.

Do I have to disclose problems when selling my Dover house?

Yes, unless the sale is exempt. Delaware's Buyer Property Protection Act requires a written disclosure of known material defects, with exemptions for court-ordered transfers, foreclosure sales and certain family transfers.

Does Dover Air Force Base affect selling a house here?

It affects who is buying and when. The base's fiscal 2023 estimate counted 6,096 military and civilian personnel and an $891 million economic impact, so a share of local buyers and sellers are tied to military moves.

Where is Newark, Delaware, and what is it known for?

Newark is a city in New Castle County about 8 miles west-southwest of Wilmington and 28 miles southwest of Philadelphia, just east of the Maryland line. It sits at about 128 feet above sea level, less than a mile south of the point where Delaware, Maryland and Pennsylvania meet.

The 2020 Census counted 30,601 residents, with a median age of 24.2, which tells you how large a part the University of Delaware plays. Main Street, the commercial center, runs next to the campus. For a house seller, the student population is the central fact of the local housing market, because it creates both a rental demand and a rulebook.

What is Newark's history and how does the university fit in?

Scots-Irish and Welsh settlers founded Newark in 1694, and King George II chartered it in 1758. Newark Academy began in 1765, and the railroad arrived in 1837. The Battle of Cooch's Bridge, fought outside Newark in the Revolutionary War, is traditionally held to be the first battle in which the Stars and Stripes were flown.

The University of Delaware traces to Newark College (1833), which merged with Newark Academy in 1834 to form Delaware College. It took its present name in 1921.

Manufacturing also left a mark. The Chrysler Newark Assembly plant opened in 1951 and employed 2,115 people in 2005 and 1,100 in 2008 before closing in late 2008. The Curtis Paper Mill, dating to about 1798, closed in 1997.

How do roads and rail connect Newark?

Interstate 95 and Delaware routes 2, 72, 273, 279 and 896 serve Newark, and the Newark rail station is served by SEPTA and Amtrak on the Northeast Corridor. DART First State and DART Connect buses use the Newark Transit Hub.

The rail link is unusual in Delaware outside Wilmington, and it brings in commuters and students who live without a car. Properties within walking distance of the station or Main Street tend to attract different buyers than houses on the outskirts, so describe your location plainly when you talk to any buyer.

Which schools serve Newark addresses?

The Christina School District runs the public schools. Elementary schools serving city limits include Downes, Maclary, McVey and West Park Place, Shue/Medill serves most of the city for middle school, and Newark High School serves almost all of it. Newark Charter School (K to 12) and the Delaware School for the Deaf are also in the area.

The city has more than 700 acres of parkland and open space, 36 parks and 21 miles of trails. Buyers often check that list when comparing houses.

What does Newark's climate mean for a house?

Newark has a humid subtropical climate in hardiness zone 7a, with about 46.96 inches of precipitation a year across roughly 110 days and more than 220 frost-free days. The mean daily high is 66.4 degrees, and recorded extremes run from 105 degrees to minus 12.

Frequent precipitation means gutters, grading and basements matter. Gather service records for the roof, furnace and sump pump if you have one.

How do Newark's rental permit and student home rules affect a sale?

Newark requires an annual rental permit for non-owner-occupied properties leased to tenants, and for owner-occupied homes that rent rooms to more than two unrelated people. Any ownership change requires an updated rental license application, even between related parties.

The rules are most specific for student homes. The city defines a student home as a single-family detached dwelling occupied by three post-secondary students unrelated by blood or adoption, and sets these conditions:

  • No more than three people may occupy a student home.
  • A student home must sit farther from any other student home than ten times the required lot width for a single-family house in that district.
  • Existing rentals with permits when the ordinance was adopted count toward that distance.
  • Thirty-three listed subdivisions and some listed streets are excluded from the definition.

Zoning caps non-owner-occupied single-family rentals at three unrelated occupants in the RH, RT, RS, RD and RR districts, or four in RM. Check your deed, since some properties have lower limits. If you are selling a house that has been used as a rental, a cash buyer who plans to keep renting must work within those rules, and an investor who wants a student home needs to confirm the distance requirement first.

What inspection and exterior rules does Newark enforce on rentals?

Newark's Code Enforcement Division requires mandatory exterior and common area inspections for rentals, and an annual inspection is required for rental units. Interior inspections are voluntary under the city's rental permit page, though other city material says annual inspections are required, so ask the division which applies.

Rules the city lists for rental properties include:

  • Refuse cans of 20 or 32 gallons, labeled with the address, with tight lids.
  • Curbside refuse under 40 pounds, set out no earlier than 6:00 p.m. the day before collection.
  • Weeds and grass notices once growth exceeds 10 inches.
  • Snow and ice cleared from the sidewalk within 24 hours, leaving a path at least three feet wide.

Leases longer than 30 days are required, and an occupant posting must be displayed inside the unit. The Code Enforcement Division is at 220 South Main Street, phone (302) 366-7000.

How are Newark property taxes billed?

Newark's city real estate tax rate for 2026 to 2027 is $0.2464 per $100 of assessed value, with bills issued after July 1 and a payment deadline of September 30, 2026 to avoid a penalty. New Castle County's Assessment Office sets the assessed value, which determines both the city and the school tax, and assessments were listed as of April 1, 2026.

If your mortgage company pays taxes from escrow, your bill is for information only. Past-due notices go out quarterly. The city says its Finance Department can answer questions at (302) 366-7000.

What does a Newark sale cost under Delaware law?

Delaware's realty transfer tax normally totals 4 percent, with 2.5 percent state tax and 1.5 percent county or municipal tax, apportioned equally between seller and buyer. A first-time buyer can trim the buyer's share by 0.5 percent of up to $400,000, or up to $2,000.

A Delaware attorney must run the settlement, and a seller of a one to four unit home must provide the written disclosure report before an offer. Utility accounts matter in Newark because the city runs its own electric department, serving about 12,800 customers, and a water system serving about 33,000 customers. A final reading and payoff keeps the settlement clean.

Do I need a rental permit to sell a Newark rental?

You need a valid permit while the house is rented, and any ownership change requires an updated rental license application, even between related parties. Contact Code Enforcement at (302) 366-7000 for the discontinuation form if the rental ends.

What is a student home in Newark?

It is a single-family detached dwelling occupied by three post-secondary students unrelated by blood or adoption. A student home must meet a distance requirement from other student homes and may have no more than three occupants.

When is Newark city property tax due?

Bills are issued after July 1 and must be paid by September 30 to avoid a penalty. For 2026 to 2027 the city rate is $0.2464 per $100 of assessed value.

Who sets assessed values for Newark properties?

New Castle County's Assessment Office sets them, and the Board of Assessment Review decides appeals. Call the county at (302) 395-5520 for appeal forms.

Is a lawyer required to close a Newark house sale?

Yes. Delaware requires a Delaware-licensed attorney to conduct real estate settlements, under the state Supreme Court's 2000 Mid-Atlantic Settlement Services decision and its 2006 order.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling a house in Middletown, Delaware comes down to listing it, selling it yourself or taking a cash offer. Each route has different costs and timelines under Delaware law. The Census Bureau estimates 25,798 residents in Middletown as of July 1, 2025.

Middletown at a glance

  • Estimated population, July 1, 2025: 25,798 (Census Bureau).
Selling in Middletown?
We buy Middletown houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Where is Middletown, Delaware, and how fast has it grown?

Middletown is a town in southern New Castle County, incorporated in 1861, at about 66 feet above sea level. Its population rose from 6,161 in 2000 to 18,871 in 2010, an increase of 206.3 percent, and reached 23,192 in the 2020 Census. Recent land annexations drove much of that growth.

Growth of that size shapes what a seller faces. Much of the housing around the old town center is recent subdivision construction, and a large share of buyers are looking at new homes from builders as well as resale houses. Your house competes with both.

The town center itself is older. Middletown's local newspaper, the Middletown Transcript, first printed on January 4, 1868, and population was only 368 in 1850, so the historic blocks are small compared with the surrounding developments.

What roads connect Middletown to Wilmington and Dover?

Middletown sits between two toll roads. The DE 1 toll road runs along the east edge of town with an exit at Odessa for DE 299, and the US 301 toll road lies just west and north with exits for DE 299 and DE 71. DE 71 runs north and south through town on Broad Street, and DE 299 runs east and west on Main Street.

DART First State bus routes serve the town, including Routes 46, 37 and 302. With no passenger rail in town, access to those highways is a selling point to describe accurately. The US 301 corridor is also where national retail and food chains have expanded.

What employers and services are near Middletown?

An Amazon fulfillment center operates in Middletown, and ChristianaCare runs a 24-hour free-standing emergency department that opened in April 2013 at a cost of $34 million. The town operates its own Electric Department and Water/Wastewater Department.

That last point matters at closing. Town utility accounts are set up for home buyers through the settlement attorneys, so no visit to Town Hall is needed, and the town's utility late fee is 6 percent once a bill is seven days past due.

  • Pay the final electric, water, sewer and trash bills before settlement.
  • Ask your attorney to request a tax and utility payoff figure from the town.
  • Keep your account number and online payment PIN handy for the final bill.

Which school district serves Middletown?

The Appoquinimink School District serves Middletown and was formed when Middletown School District 60 and Odessa School District 61 merged on July 1, 1969. Its high schools include Middletown High School, Appoquinimink High School (opened 2008) and Odessa High School (opened 2020).

St. Georges Technical High School lies northeast of town, and private options include St. Anne's Episcopal School and St. Andrew's School. Many sellers find that school boundaries are the first question from family buyers, so confirm which school your address feeds before you list.

What weather should a Middletown seller plan for?

Middletown averages about 41.68 inches of precipitation and 14.5 inches of snow a year, with a mean daily high of 66 degrees and a mean daily low of 45. Records run from 104 degrees in summer to minus 15 in winter.

That range is hard on roofs, gutters and heating systems. A buyer's inspector will look at roof age and attic ventilation, and a dated furnace is a common negotiation point. Photos of recent repairs and service receipts help a seller document the house.

How do Middletown property taxes work?

Middletown bills a town property tax based on New Castle County assessed value, and New Castle County and the school district bill their own taxes separately. The town mails its bills around August 1, and payment must reach the Town Tax Office by September 30 to avoid penalties. A 1.5 percent penalty applies for each month a bill is overdue.

Seniors 65 and older who have lived in town at least a year may apply once for a discount, with the application due before July 1 for that tax year. The discount attaches to the residence, so a new owner must reapply.

New Castle County reassessed property countywide in 2025, the first such reassessment since 1983, so a seller's current assessed value may be very different from what the last owner paid. Check yours on the county's parcel search before you set expectations. The town's tax page lists two different rates in different places, so ask the Tax Office for the current figure.

What rental rules apply if you are selling a Middletown rental?

Middletown requires owners of rental property to register with the town and have the unit inspected at each change of tenant. The first inspection costs $75, one re-inspection is free, and the unit must be vacant and clean. Rental properties must be re-registered every three years from approval, and owners of two or more rental units, along with authorized agents, need a town business license.

The town's Clean Hands Ordinance means past-due bills and fees at the property must be paid before an inspection can be scheduled. Utility service for a tenant requires a passed town inspection and a $300 deposit, and only electric and trash can go in the tenant's name, while water and sewer stay with the owner.

  • A mobile home buyer cannot set up service until the previous owner's taxes are paid in full.
  • Notify the town in writing of changes in rental information.
  • Ask the town about transfer steps, since its procedures do not spell out ownership changes.

What should a Middletown seller gather before asking for offers?

Start with the paperwork that every Delaware sale needs, because gaps here slow a closing more than anything about the house itself. Having these items ready lets a cash buyer or a listing agent move quickly.

  • Your deed and the name of the closing attorney you will use.
  • The most recent town tax bill and the New Castle County assessed value from the parcel search.
  • Final utility readings for electric, water, sewer and trash, which the town bills itself.
  • The Seller's Disclosure of Real Property Condition Report, completed honestly, with radon information if you have any.
  • If the house is a rental, the town registration, the last passed inspection and tenant notices.

If the house came to you through an estate, the disclosure exemption for fiduciary transfers may apply, and your attorney can confirm it. Delaware's disclosure law also notes that a completed form is a good-faith effort and not a warranty, so complete it carefully but do not treat it as a substitute for the buyer's own inspection.

What does a Middletown sale cost and require under Delaware law?

The usual Delaware realty transfer tax is 4 percent, with 2.5 percent state tax and 1.5 percent county or municipal tax, split equally between seller and buyer by statute. The state's first-time homebuyer reduction trims the buyer's share by 0.5 percent of up to $400,000, a maximum of $2,000.

A Delaware-licensed attorney must conduct the settlement, and sellers of homes with one to four units must give the Seller's Disclosure of Real Property Condition Report before an offer. Nonresident individuals pay estimated tax of 6.6 percent of the gain with Form REW EST when the deed is recorded.

A cash sale lets you set a closing date, but these steps apply to any route. We buy as-is and do not quote a price before seeing the property.

More questions about Middletown, DE

When are Middletown property taxes due?

The Town of Middletown mails bills around August 1 and they must reach the Tax Office by September 30 to avoid penalties. A 1.5 percent penalty applies for each month a bill is overdue.

Who sets my assessed value in Middletown?

New Castle County sets assessed value, and the town applies its rate to that figure. The county completed a countywide reassessment in 2025, the first since 1983.

Do I need to inspect a Middletown rental before tenants move out or in?

Yes. The town requires an inspection at each change of tenant, with a $75 first inspection fee and one free re-inspection. Past-due bills at the property must be paid before scheduling.

How do utilities transfer when I sell a Middletown house?

Account setup for the buyer is handled through the settlement attorneys. As the seller, pay your final bills first, because late charges of 6 percent apply once a bill is seven days past due.

Which school district is Middletown in?

The Appoquinimink School District serves Middletown, with Middletown High School, Appoquinimink High School and Odessa High School among its high schools.
